summary: The five delivered records always select C, bypassing its classification. This is a finite-batch selection defect; the broader generator varies C. Other seven checks passed.

source_analysis.skill: Identify ordinary matrices in row echelon form, or its complement, by checking leading-entry positions and placement of zero rows.
reasoning_steps: Locate zero rows and leading entries.
Check both row echelon conditions for each matrix.
Select exactly the qualifying labels; explain a concrete violation for rejected matrices.
invariants: Zero rows must be below all nonzero rows.
Leading columns strictly increase down the nonzero rows.
Leading entries need not equal one; entries above pivots need not vanish.
Each field key, solution matrix, selection truth and requested polarity must agree.
Retain source banks and response type when replaying each source.
permitted_variations: Change nonzero values, signs and entries to the right of pivots while deriving explanations.
Change zero-row location, pivot-column sequences (increasing, repeated, decreasing), dimensions within comparable workload.
Reassign qualifying status to any label or shape; neither A/B/C nor source profile determines truth.
Vary in/not-in polarity and subset size, including source-observed all-three cases; do not fix eligible qualifying labels.
Reorder presentations and fields without stale labels, keys or solutions.

source_replay.details: All 13 complete easy checkbox sources replayed with full banks and verified corrections. Incomplete unrated radio and bankless canonical example are explicitly bounded.

math.details: Independent classification of 416 sampled records and all five runner records found no key or solution-matrix errors; 252 explicit pivot witnesses verified.

variety.details: All seven nonempty subsets occur within every supported profile, including after delivery deduplication. This sampler-level result does not waive the exact-batch shortcut.

scope.details: Ordinary small integer matrices; both lesson conditions; no new operators, row operations or reduced-echelon requirement.

grading.details: Native learner grader passed 180 checks: 90 accepted correct states and 90 rejected opposite states. Checkbox response contract has no free-entry equivalents.

rendering.details: 12 actual-UI renderings passed; representative screenshots inspected, including relevant and irrelevant edits.

packaging.details: Exact Python 3.13.5 and empty third-party dependency map verified. Relocation, deterministic replay, input rejection and package immutability passed.

decision_variation.details: Runner subsets ABC, BC, BC, AC, AC leave C selected 5/5 before and after delivery. Always selecting C correctly answers that field without inspecting its matrix, including 4/4 select-echelon items. A/B still require classification. Larger control has 180 C-unselected survivors. Five stored non-source records reproduce the same finite-subset pattern; full captured bank is not universally affected.

findings.description: The exact five-record practice batch fixes the selected role at label C. A learner can always check C and bypass one of three intended independent classifications. This is a batch/pool selection failure, not a universal generator defect or an incorrect individual answer. Five captured non-source stored records also always select C; affected-inventory.json identifies their reproduced normalized UUIDs.
findings.reproduction: python3 batch_role_probe.py delivery-batch/accepted.json batch-role-results.json exits 1: C selected=5, unselected=0. Exact dependency example: seed 924724049, profile q-129214, C=[[-2,-2,-2,-1],[0,3,-5,5],[0,0,0,7]]. Changing only c21 from 0 to 1 correctly changes ABC to AB; run c_counterfactual.py and its saved native-grader cases.
findings.requested_change: Revise finite-batch/pool construction to prevent a visible label from supplying a fixed correct checkbox action across every delivered item. Replace enough members with valid same-method instances where C is unselected, deriving all dependent content and keys. Retain the strict batch-role regression and rerun it after actual delivery filtering; do not narrow the broader sampler or change the REF rule.
